clue.text: Painter, Italian one cast in bronze

indicators.note: something cast in a material is enclosed by it, so the first letters go inside the metal

blocks.note: IT is the standard abbreviation for Italian
the Roman numeral for one
bronze as a colour, or a suntan

explanation.surface: An Italian painter is being commemorated with a bronze statue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast in bronze' reads as a statue, but 'cast in' is the instruction to enclose the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great sixteenth-century Venetian painter, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Temperature round roof of penthouse flat of the highest order

indicators.note: the roof is the top of a building, so only the first letter of the word in a down clue is wanted

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
a round shape is the letter O
the opening letter of penthouse
flat and level both mean even, without slopes

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb: the temperature around the roof of a penthouse flat is first-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like the home that has the penthouse, but it is the adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-level means senior or most important, the same rank as something of the highest order.

indicators.note: foreign things are strange and unfamiliar, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar order

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that foreign exchange has been set right in a chaotic, bungled way.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-ring circus is a scene of noisy confusion with too much going on, which is what a shambles is.

blocks.note: taken as written
to mount is to climb up something

explanation.surface: Someone asking how far up a climb goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount is a quantity or total, the size or extent of something.

indicators.note: disrupted things are thrown out of their usual order, so the letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatre interval was cut short by some disturbance in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTR'ACTE, French for 'between acts', is written here without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is the break between acts of a play, or music played during that break.

clue.text: Fool emerging from small hotel in New York

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside, so the hotel sits within the city's letters

blocks.note: NY is the standard abbreviation for New York
an inn is a small hotel or pub with rooms

explanation.surface: A clown is seen stepping out of a little hotel in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emerging from' only joins the definition to the wordplay, which yields the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninny is a silly, foolish person, a mild synonym for fool.

clue.text: Wine, drop of red that is given to cast

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only one letter, the first, is taken from the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of red
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is
to sling is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: A wine with a splash of red added is handed to the cast of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape variety and the wine made from it, especially in Germany and Alsace.

clue.text: Lawyer hit over the head plain court is shaken

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled about, so the letters of the word before it are mixed up

blocks.note: to crown someone, informally, is to hit them on the head
prose is plain ordinary writing, not verse
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer was attacked over the head and the courtroom is left trembling.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Crown is the state in criminal cases, so a Crown prosecutor brings cases on its behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: A Crown prosecutor is a lawyer who prosecutes criminal cases for the state in Britain and Commonwealth countries.

blocks.note: to end is to stop
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: The final halt on a Yorkshire river cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like the adjective final; it is the verb meaning to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or survive over time, which is what endure means.

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful or permitted, so acceptable

explanation.surface: Someone confirms they have understood that a single member is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood without being said outright, implied rather than stated.

blocks.note: a show is a performance
a bond is a tie or union

explanation.surface: A demand that the trade union produce a written guarantee.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance bond is a surety, often from a bank, guaranteeing that a contractor will complete the work as agreed.

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a tern is a seabird
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A sentimental line about an English bird being a companion for life.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means without end, always, which is the sense of the adverbial phrase for ever.

blocks.note: a line is a course or route taken
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A boat on a river is keeping to its course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the river's letter after the course, as across clues read left to right.
explanation.definitionFit: A liner is a large passenger ship, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Girl is to eat on the way back

indicators.note: going back retraces the route in the opposite direction, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: A girl is going to stop for a meal on her journey home.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a girl's name, as with the children's author Enid Blyton.

blocks.note: first meaning: a fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel with two or more masts
second meaning: a large glass for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: A ship in a bottle, the classic model built inside glass.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a schooner is a tall sherry glass; in Australia and the US it is a beer glass.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a type of rigged sailing vessel and a particular drinking glass for sherry or beer.

blocks.note: overt means open and plain to see
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether something blatant can really carry a secret message.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets obvious against hidden, while the answer joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a subtle additional implication or connotation, a meaning suggested beneath the literal one.

blocks.note: turns are acts or routines on stage
a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A one-time employee performs while feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit was a kitchen servant, historically a boy or dog, who turned the roasting spit, a job long gone.

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
to press is to crush or squeeze

explanation.surface: A menu choice between a drink, a crush or a squash, all fruit drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Crush and squash are British soft drinks, which disguises the verb sense of both.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash a rebellion or rumour is to suppress it, putting it down by force.

clue.text: Glove female relative left in bag

indicators.note: placing something in another thing puts it inside, so the relative and the side go within the word for bag

blocks.note: an aunt is a female relative
L is the abbreviation for left
to bag something is to get or capture it

explanation.surface: A glove belonging to an aunt was left behind in a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the verb (forgotten), but it is the abbreviation for the side; 'bag' is the verb meaning to obtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a strong glove with a long, wide cuff, so a type of glove.

indicators.note: the answer is literally inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A Bible quiz question wondering whether Jacob's twin was Saul.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul is a red herring, another Old Testament figure; the answer sits across the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Esau is Jacob's elder twin brother, who sold his birthright for a meal.

clue.text: Char or cleaner's first in school

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the word just before it
being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within the abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of cleaner
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A school cleaner, a char in British slang, is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is old British slang for a cleaning lady, which the surface leans on; here it is the verb meaning to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: To char something is to burn its surface black, which is what scorch means.

clue.text: Information on girl from European city

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Intelligence about a young woman has come from a city on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the information above the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a Swiss city on Lake Geneva, home to many international organisations.

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and crazy letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog left in a car is barking its head off.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like what the dog does, but it is the British slang for crazy, short for barking mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn terrier is a small Scottish breed, so a cairn is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Plant about to be planted in flatter environment?

indicators.note: something planted in soil is set inside it, so the small piece goes within the longer phrase
an environment is the surroundings of something, so the phrase is placed around the small piece

blocks.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A plant is about to be set out in a nice level bed in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'planted' make it look like gardening throughout, and 'flatter' poses as a comparison of level ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a common wild flower with bright yellow cup-shaped petals.

indicators.note: being in a building means being inside it, so the number goes within the outbuilding

blocks.note: a barn is a farm building, like a stable
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A child born in a stable, recalling the Nativity.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside BARN, after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scots and northern English word for a child.

clue.text: Focus on party providing temporary shelter

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another follows it, so the first-named piece is written second

blocks.note: a reception is a formal party
a centre is a focus or focal point

explanation.surface: The organisers concentrate on a party that will put people up for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Focus on party' puts the focus after the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception centre is a place where refugees or homeless people are housed briefly, a temporary shelter.

clue.text: Reluctant male has to take a seat next to social worker

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
to sit is to take a seat
an ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A reluctant man is made to sit down beside a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: A social worker is an ant: ants live in colonies and most are workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant means unwilling or slow to act, holding back, just as reluctant does.

clue.text: Sign he's cut out of reference book

indicators.note: cutting something out of a whole removes it, leaving the rest of the word

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
a thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms

explanation.surface: A man signals that he has been edited out of a reference work.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.
